limit_scope: MAIN TEXT ONLY, at the time of initial submission. Counted from page 1 through the last page of main-text prose (the main text ends before the bibliography). Raised to 10 pages for the discussion/rebuttal phase and for the camera-ready version.
excluded_from_limit: references / bibliography (explicitly: unlimited additional pages allowed)
appendices (unlimited, must be placed after the bibliography)
supplementary material / supplementary text (appears after the references)
Ethics Statement (optional; does not count, but must not exceed 1 page)
Reproducibility Statement (optional; explicitly 'not part of the main text')
Acknowledgements section (FAQ answers 'No' to whether it is included in the page limit)
LLM-usage disclosure section (new for 2026; may be placed in the appendix and does not count)
counts_toward_limit: all main-text sections: abstract, introduction, related work, method, experiments, results, analysis, discussion, limitations
all figures and tables placed in the main text
fetch_method: curl -L via http://hy-proxy.woa.com:3128 (WebFetch tool refuses the iclr.cc domain)
verbatim_quote:
Paper length

At the time of submission, the main text should be 9 pages or fewer. During the discussion/rebuttal phase and for the camera ready, the page limit will be increased to 10 pages to allow for new results/discussions. This limit will be strictly enforced. Papers with main text beyond the page limit will be desk-rejected.

The list of references does not count towards the page limit, and unlimited additional pages are allowed for the bibliography/references.

Authors may use as many pages of appendices (after the bibliography) as they wish, but reviewers are not required to read the appendix.

ethics_statement.quote: The optional ethics statement will not count toward the page limit, but should not be more than 1 page.
ethics_statement.context_quote: If authors feel that their paper submission raises questions regarding the Code of Ethics, they are encouraged to include a paragraph of Ethics Statement (at the end of the main text before references) to address potential concerns where appropriate.

reproducibility_statement.quote: This optional reproducibility statement is not part of the main text and therefore will not count toward the page limit.
reproducibility_statement.context_quote: Authors are strongly encouraged to include a paragraph-long Reproducibility Statement at the end of the main text (before references) to discuss the efforts that have been made to ensure reproducibility.

references.quote: The list of references does not count towards the page limit, and unlimited additional pages are allowed for the bibliography/references.

appendix.quote: Authors may use as many pages of appendices (after the bibliography) as they wish, but reviewers are not required to read the appendix.

acknowledgements.quote:
Q. Is the acknowledgement section included in the page limit?
No.
acknowledgements.note: FAQ Re:submission section. Also stated under Camera-ready Submissions: 'Similarly, ethics statements and acknowledgement etc. do not count for page limit.'

llm_usage_section.quote: This section can appear in the appendix, and will not be considered as part of the page limit.
llm_usage_section.context_quote: However, new this year, if LLMs played a significant role in research ideation and/or writing to the extent that they could be regarded as a contributor, then authors should describe the precise role of the LLM in a separate section on LLM usage.

camera_ready.quote:
page limit is identical with the submission version (10 pages)
Similarly, ethics statements and acknowledgement etc. do not count for page limit.

notes: AMBIGUITY 1 (which number to size against): the guide gives TWO numbers for the same paper at different lifecycle stages -- 9 at initial submission, 10 during rebuttal and camera-ready. For a compliance fix aimed at submission, the binding number is 9. Sizing to 10 would pass camera-ready but be desk-rejected at submission.

AMBIGUITY 2 (which year is live): ICLR 2026's deadline has passed and its OpenReview submission invitation returns InvitationExpiredError. If paperC targets a real venue, that venue is ICLR 2027, whose rule is textually identical, so limit_pages = 9 holds regardless. But the paperC directory's style files say 2026, which will render 'Under review as a conference paper at ICLR 2026' -- a year mismatch to resolve separately from the page count.

AMBIGUITY 3 (where the main text 'ends'): the guide says the Ethics and Reproducibility statements go 'at the end of the main text before references' yet are not counted. So a page that mixes counted main text with an excluded statement is genuinely ambiguous to count. The safe reading (and what a PC page-counter would do) is: keep counted main text within 9 pages and place excluded statements so they do not push counted content onto page 10.

The Author Guide fetch behaved differently from the user's reported CFP fetch: our CFP fetch returned the full 49.7 KB page, not a 3835-char stub. The stub was likely a transient proxy/CDN artifact. Either way the CFP genuinely contains no page-limit text, so following the author-guide link was necessary, not optional.

The task brief hypothesised the OpenReview submission invitation's description/webfield would state the limit. MEASURED: it does not -- the venue group webfield is only JS tab logic, and the invitation itself is expired. Do not rely on OpenReview for ICLR page limits.

The .sty file legitimately contains no page-limit text (confirmed: paperC's copy is byte-identical to the official one, md5 a040392a6cfee8dc54aae17eb2635282). Grepping the .sty is not a valid way to discover the limit for any ICLR year.
